ev.q: In 2023, at least 13 children in Utah became ill during an outbreak of Shiga toxin–producing Escherichia coli O157:H7
Nearly all children (12 of 13) reported using this untreated water for unintended purposes, including recreation and drinking.
Seven patients were hospitalized, including two with HUS; no deaths were reported.
Cases of reported Shiga toxin–producing Escherichia coli O157:H7 illnesses, by onset date* (N = 13)
Twelve of 13 ill persons reported UPMIW exposure in city A during the week before symptom onset
Investigators identified 13 children with confirmed STEC O157:H7 illness linked to this outbreak
the environmental isolates were all within 0–2 allele differences of the clinical isolates by core genome multilocus sequence typing

public_health_question.v: What was the source of a 2023 STEC O157:H7 outbreak among children in a Utah city, and how can untreated municipal irrigation water–associated illness be prevented?

ev.q: linked the illnesses to untreated, pressurized, municipal irrigation water (UPMIW) exposure in city A

conditions.v: Shiga toxin–producing Escherichia coli O157:H7 illness

ev.q: Shiga Toxin–Producing Escherichia coli O157:H7 Illness Outbreak Associated with Untreated, Pressurized, Municipal Irrigation Water
Seven children were hospitalized, including two with hemolytic uremic syndrome.
On July 31, an outbreak investigation was initiated.
UCHD investigators interviewed the identified children’s parents using standard case investigation forms
six cases of STEC O157:H7 illness in children were reported to the Utah County Health Department (UCHD)
Investigators collected large-volume water samples by dead-end ultrafiltration and grab samples

equity.level_reason: Only age defines the population (children); no other social-position dimension is analyzed or framed.

ev.q: The median patient age was 4 years (range = 1–15 years).

notes: Read as a descriptive outbreak case series with environmental lab results; no exposed vs unexposed comparison or attack rates. The observation that two STEC-positive sites had undetectable coliforms is a lab indicator finding, not an analytic comparison. Microbial source tracking and WGS are laboratory methods supporting source attribution, not procedures.
